title: Non-Invertible Symmetries Mixing with Witt Non-Trivial Quantum Cellular Automata
authors: Kansei Inamura, Oskar Wojdel, Lukasz Fidkowski, Sakura Schafer-Nameki
abstract: Self-dualities and the stacking of symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases are basic operations on quantum many-body systems. For a $\mathbb{Z}_p$ one-form symmetry in 3+1d these correspond to the Kramers-Wannier-Wegner duality $S$, which is the gauging operation underlying non-invertible duality symmetries, and the stacking of a 1-form symmetry SPT $T$. In the continuum, they form a central extension of $PSL(2,\mathbb{Z}_4)$ for $p=2$, and of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z}_p)$ for odd primes $p$, whose central elements are invertible theories with purely gravitational response. These central extensions are governed by a twisted, graded generalization of the Witt group of abelian anyon theories, which we determine. For $p=2$ the resulting group is the single-qubit Clifford group, with duality and entangler acting as the Hadamard and phase gates. We realize this entire structure microscopically as quantum cellular automata (QCA) acting on a certain local operator algebra associated with a spin lattice Hilbert space on a cubic lattice. Specifically, our local operator algebra is built by starting with all local operators commuting with a $\mathbb{Z}_p$ 1-form symmetry, and taking the quotient by all the (local) 1-form symmetry generators. The central elements can always be extended to the full tensor product algebra with a uniquely defined QCA class. For $p=2$ they are generated by the non-trivial semion QCA, and for odd prime $p$ they are generated by the non-trivial $\mathbb{Z}_p$ Clifford QCA. Consequently the lattice fusion rules reproduce the continuum ones only up to these QCAs and lattice translations, giving rise to fusion rules refined by QCAs.
summary: This theoretical paper investigates how non-invertible symmetries, particularly those involving duality, manifest on quantum lattices. By comparing continuum predictions from Witt group theory with explicit constructions using Quantum Cellular Automata, the authors characterize the underlying algebraic structure governing these exotic symmetries in 3+1 dimensions.
main_problem: The paper addresses constructing a lattice framework for non-invertible symmetries, particularly those involving duality operations, in quantum many-body systems.
main_result: It establishes that the group of locality-preserving automorphisms on the lattice matches predictions from advanced categorical calculations (the pointed Witt group), identifying specific Quantum Cellular Automata (QCA) generators for these symmetries.
method: The authors use algebraic methods, comparing continuum defect relations derived from the graded Witt group with explicit constructions using local operator algebras and QCA acting on spin lattices.
model_or_system: The study focuses on quantum many-body systems exhibiting a Zp one-form symmetry in 3+1 dimensions. The mathematical machinery involves analyzing automorphisms of constrained local spin operator algebras built upon a cubic lattice structure.
key_observables: The group structure of locality-preserving automorphisms, which is related to the Clifford group for p=2 and SL(2, Zp) for odd primes p.
important_parameters: The symmetry parameter p (prime), the dimensionality (3+1d), and the specific form of the symmetry ($\mathbb{Z}_p$ 1-form).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on conjectures regarding the full group of automorphisms modulo finite depth circuits, and some proofs are noted to fall short of rigor.
figures_summary: Not specified in detail, but notes reference Tables I and II comparing continuum defect theory relations with lattice operators (KWW, TW).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the symmetry problem using $\mathbb{Z}_p$ 1-form symmetries, then calculating the expected group structure via Witt groups, and finally realizing this structure microscopically through specific Quantum Cellular Automata acting on local operator algebras.
why_interesting: It provides a deep connection between abstract algebraic structures (Witt groups) and concrete physical realizations in lattice models (QCA), which is crucial for understanding topological order beyond simple symmetry protection.
